title: Shaping the Curve
identity: Michael Nyman’s Shaping the Curve (1990) is for soprano saxophone and piano, published by Chester Music. IRCAM records the work and scoring. Hal Leonard’s composer/product information says it was composed for John Harle and built on a four-chord sequence. The Royal Irish Academy of Music lists it in both saxophone Teacher and Performer diploma repertoires.

evidence.claim: IRCAM identifies the 1990 work, Chester Music, and soprano saxophone/piano instrumentation.
Composer/publisher product description identifies John Harle as dedicatee/commissioning performer and describes the work as based on a four-chord sequence.
evidence.source_name: Hal Leonard / Chester Music product record

evidence.claim: Royal Irish Academy of Music’s ARIAM/LRIAM wind syllabus lists Shaping the Curve in the saxophone Teacher repertoire and, separately, in the Performer diploma repertoire; performer candidates give a varied recital of up to 50 minutes.
evidence.source_name: Royal Irish Academy of Music ARIAM/LRIAM syllabus

review_focus: Inference from the composer/publisher note: examine how phrase length, harmonic pacing, and soprano-sax/piano balance operate over the recurring four-chord sequence. The RIAM source confirms diploma programming, not a college-year assignment.
collection_flag: Soprano saxophone/piano work composed for John Harle and listed in Royal Irish Academy of Music Teacher and Performer diploma repertoires.
